text: When this chapter is placed beside the earlier promise, the difference between them is narrowed. Readers are reminded that Isaac is the child of the covenant, the one through whom the nations are to be blessed; and the covenant promise, thus recalled, is made the substance of a test. The scene turns upon the single Hebrew word _hineni_, "here I am," spoken three times by Abraham, once to God, once to Isaac, and once to the angel. In each use the word has a different force, and in each use it costs him more; presence here cannot be severed from loss for Abraham.
